_comment: Ignore rules for the statediff drift sweep (importer/kit/statediff.py, --ignore).
Every rule needs a 'reason': an unexplained ignore is indistinguishable from a
forgotten one, and this file is the reviewed record of what the sweep is allowed
These are the GENERIC seeds — resources every AWS estate has that are managed
outside Terraform by construction. A deployment adds its own rows for its own
bootstrap resources (the state bucket and lock table named in its backend.tf,
typically as kind 'id'); those are estate-specific and do not belong in a public

rules.reason: Applied by EC2 Auto Scaling to every instance it launches. It is not writable from Terraform, so it appears as drift on every ASG-managed instance forever.
Stamped by CloudFormation on resources it owns. A Terraform-managed estate that still has CFN stacks will otherwise report every one of their resources as drift.
Stamped by Elastic Beanstalk on the resources it provisions; not settable from Terraform.
Service-linked roles are created by AWS services on demand and cannot be managed by Terraform; they are deleted with the service, not by the estate.
AWS-managed policies are owned by AWS. They are referenced by the estate but never declared in it.
Created implicitly by Lambda on first invocation when the estate has not declared the group explicitly. Declare the group to remove the need for this row.
